sourcePolicy: Relative paths refer to the same pinned revision as this digest-covered export. Historical references and private runs are not published ports.

targetVersions: ChatGPT desktop app with Settings > Appearance import (2026-09)

verification.reason: No recorded real-import protocol bound to this subject.

appearance-settings.reason: Mode, accent, background, foreground, contrast, UI and code font size, reduce motion, separate light and dark, diff markers, and the diff and skill colours in the import string.

text-ladder.reason: One global foreground: prose, muted, subtle and disabled text follow ChatGPT's own derivation.

surfaces.reason: One background; ChatGPT derives its other surfaces.

interaction.reason: Focus and state colours follow the accent.

status-colours.reason: Only diff added, diff removed and skill have colours.

code-colours.reason: Syntax colours come from the code theme ChatGPT offers.

typography.reason: Only two sizes; fonts stay the system default.

geometry.reason: ChatGPT keeps its own rounded corners and focus ring; j3w1's zero radius and dashed focus ring cannot be set.

files.install: Open ChatGPT > Settings > Appearance > Dark theme > Import and paste a preset's import string, or set the values in the preset's table by hand (see ports/chatgpt/README.md).

ports.rollback: In ChatGPT: Settings > Appearance, import the theme copied before, or choose another theme and set back each row of the preset table that was changed. Nothing is installed on disk.

theme-roles.reason: Claude Code's custom theme (base dark-ansi) sets these roles: text and accents, message backgrounds, input and dialog borders, status, diff lines, the usage meter and subagent names.

terminal-palette.reason: Claude Code runs in a terminal and uses its sixteen slots, background and cursor; the terminal's own theme sets them.

fixed-ansi.reason: Highlighted code, links (slot 12), diff + and - markers and file previews use fixed ANSI slots that no theme reaches.

light-mode.reason: The theme has no light profile; the custom theme is dark (base dark-ansi) in every mode.

outside-claude.reason: Roles Claude Code's theme has no key for: primitives, interface colours of other components and every value that is not a colour.

files.install: Save as ~/.claude/themes/j3w1.json and set "theme": "custom:j3w1" in ~/.claude/settings.json; or run node ports/claude-code/install.mjs apply in a clone of this repository (see its README).

ports.rollback: Run node ports/claude-code/install.mjs restore in the same clone. By hand: set "theme" in ~/.claude/settings.json back to your previous theme (or remove the key) and delete ~/.claude/themes/j3w1.json.

verification.reason: No recorded real-import protocol bound to this subject.

theme-scopes.reason: Codex colours highlighted code from the tmTheme's scope foregrounds and bold, and tints added and removed diff lines with the markup.inserted and markup.deleted backgrounds.

editor-surfaces.reason: Codex paints no code background, current line, selection, gutter or find highlight from a tmTheme, and no modified-line tint; the file still carries those values.

font-styles.reason: Codex renders only bold from a tmTheme: comments are not italic, and links and invalid text are not underlined.

fixed-ansi.reason: Status, diff signs, the brand and the status line use ANSI slots 1-6 that Codex names; the prompt and composer fills are computed from the terminal background.

terminal-palette.reason: Codex runs in a terminal and uses its sixteen slots and background; the terminal's own theme sets them.

outside-codex.reason: Roles a tmTheme has no key for: primitives, interface colours and every value that is not a colour.

files.install: Save as ~/.codex/themes/j3w1.tmTheme and set theme = "j3w1" under [tui] in ~/.codex/config.toml; or run node ports/codex/install.mjs apply in a clone of this repository (see its README).

ports.rollback: Run node ports/codex/install.mjs restore in the same clone. By hand: set theme under [tui] in ~/.codex/config.toml back to your previous theme (or remove the line) and delete ~/.codex/themes/j3w1.tmTheme.

terminal-colours.reason: Import from Ghostty writes background, foreground, cursor, cursor text and all sixteen palette slots as Orca colour overrides.

terminal-selection.reason: Import from Ghostty writes the selection background and foreground overrides.

pane-divider.reason: Import from Ghostty writes split-divider-color to Orca's dark and light divider colours.

terminal-font.reason: Import from Ghostty writes the terminal font family and size (px).

terminal-line-height.reason: Orca keeps its own line height and letter spacing.

light-mode.reason: The theme has no light profile. Orca's colour overrides apply whatever terminal theme is selected, so they are a dark theme in either mode.

outside-terminal.reason: Application window, sidebar and settings chrome are not themed by a terminal theme file.

files.install: Save as %APPDATA%\ghostty\config.ghostty (Windows) or ~/.config/ghostty/config.ghostty, then Orca → Settings → Terminal → Import from Ghostty → Apply Changes.

ports.rollback: In Orca, open Settings → Terminal and choose "Reset all color overrides"; set the font family, font size and divider colours back to your previous values. Remove or rename %APPDATA%\ghostty\config.ghostty so a later Ghostty import does not re-apply it.

verification.reason: The cloud route was exercised; opening the files directly was not. Linux and macOS Telegram Desktop were not observed. Colours Telegram fixes in code, listed in IMPLEMENTATION.md, are outside the theme. This record names Android as its platform. The Windows Desktop check was made on the byte-identical Desktop file before D-035, which changes no Desktop key. The D-035 re-check covered the message field and outgoing messages, not rich-editor or code-block selections; D-035 records their limits.

interface.reason: Chat lists, settings, profiles, search, message text and app chrome use canonical rose text on dark surfaces.

messages.reason: Dark incoming/outgoing bubbles, selection, replies, links, metadata and media controls are colour-mapped.

controls.reason: Composer, menus, dialogs, attachment and emoji panel chrome, focus-colour hooks and translucent selectors are mapped.

wallpaper.reason: Two existing dark surface roles produce a static Android wallpaper and a 1×2 Desktop RGB background.

typography.reason: Telegram owns family, weight, size and line metrics; bold keeps the text role.

geometry.reason: Native theme formats expose colours, not square radii, border widths, focus-ring shapes or spacing.

motion.reason: Telegram controls motion and reduced-motion preferences; no animated wallpaper is emitted.

content-data.reason: Photos, videos, user accents, chart data and Premium/story artwork remain host content.

developer-surfaces.reason: This interface port has no terminal palette, diagnostic/diff model or hued syntax opt-in.

primitives.reason: Only semantic role mappings are eligible for delivery.

files.install: File install: open in Telegram for Android (or send to Saved Messages and tap), then Apply. The cloud link in the guide, when published, installs the same theme with automatic updates.
File install: open with Telegram Desktop, then Apply this theme and Keep changes. The cloud link in the guide, when published, installs the same theme with automatic updates.

ports.rollback: Choose the previous Telegram theme in Settings → Chat Settings/Appearance; restore the previous chat background if it was customised.

ports.displayName: Warp theme YAML (also Orca's Import from YAML)

verification.reason: No recorded real-import protocol bound to this subject.

terminal-colours.reason: Background, foreground, cursor, accent and all sixteen ANSI slots. Orca's Import from YAML reads background, foreground, cursor and the slots, and ignores accent when cursor is present.

terminal-selection.reason: The Warp theme format carries no selection colours.

pane-divider.reason: The Warp theme format carries no divider colour.

terminal-font.reason: Fonts are the application's own setting.

light-mode.reason: The theme has no light profile.

outside-terminal.reason: Application window, sidebar and settings chrome are not themed by a terminal theme file.

files.install: Orca → Settings → Terminal Themes → Import from YAML (or save into %APPDATA%\warp\Warp\data\themes\ and use Import from Warp), then select "j3w1 theme" as the Dark Theme. Warp: save into its themes folder.

ports.rollback: Orca: select your previous Dark Theme in Settings → Terminal Themes and remove the imported "j3w1 theme". Warp: select another theme and delete j3w1.yaml from its themes folder.
